# 3.2 · Logistic Classifier

`Level 3: Classic ML, No Excuses` · `+20 XP` · `drill 2 of 3`

## The job
Build a binary classifier. `sigmoid(z)` must survive z = -1000 and z = 1000 without an
overflow. `bce(p, y)` is binary cross-entropy with p clipped away from 0 and 1. The
`LogisticRegression` class learns weights and a bias by gradient descent in `fit`, then
offers `predict_proba`, `predict` (with a threshold) and `loss`.

## Why it matters
This is the output layer of every yes/no model, from spam filters to the reward models used
to tune chatbots. The overflow-safe sigmoid and the clipped log are the same numerical care
that keeps large models from producing NaN losses at 3 a.m.

## Run it

```bash
python fullsend.py check 3.2     # judge your drill.py
python fullsend.py hint 3.2      # one hint at a time
```

<details><summary>All hints (try the drill first)</summary>

1. Stable sigmoid: for z >= 0 use 1 / (1 + e^-z); for z < 0 use e^z / (1 + e^z). Neither branch ever exponentiates a large positive number.
2. Clip p into [eps, 1 - eps] before taking logs.
3. The gradient of mean BCE with respect to weight j is mean((p - y) * x_j). The bias gets mean(p - y).
4. `fit` should return self so you can write `LogisticRegression().fit(X, y).predict(X)`.

</details>
